description.html: Coconut coir is made from the fibers and husk of the coconut and is one of the most widely used natural terrarium substrates. It absorbs moisture and releases it slowly, helping to keep humidity stable. That makes it a good choice for species that need a more humid environment, such as crested geckos, chameleons, day geckos, tropical snakes and frogs.
It is soft and loose, so animals can dig and make burrows. It can be used on its own or mixed with sphagnum peat, and in bioactive terrariums it serves as a base for dry leaves, bark and plants.

Spread the coir across the terrarium floor and moisten it lightly so it is damp but not wet. The 5-liter pack is enough for a small terrarium or for topping up existing substrate. Remove droppings and food leftovers regularly, and replace the substrate when it starts to compact or smell. Offer insects from a bowl so the animal does not swallow substrate along with its prey.
